title: POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC pilot sync
summary: Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private VPC pilot. Reviewed networking staging results, routing workarounds for multi-AZ egress, upcoming runtime upgrade schedule, and security checklist items. Agreed next steps: run end-to-end benchmark with canary traffic, provide updated network diagram and security docs, and schedule maintenance window for runtime patch on 2027-02-24.

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-17 | Start: 17:00 UTC | Duration: ~45m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Tom Reyes (Orchid Infra Lead), Maya Singh (Orchid Security), Jules Park (Orchid ML), Liam O'Connor (Product)

[00:00] Alex: hey everyone thanks for joining, um we got about 45 minutes on the calendar, quick agenda recap - networking updates, runtime upgrade, security checklist, and next steps, cool?
[00:28] Tom: yep, sounds good. quick thing before we start — we did the staging peering test last night, results were mixed. some egress flows still go through the public nat in one az.
[00:46] Priya: ok that's what we expected, thanks for running it. on our side we saw the same — traffic from the inference workers in az-b was routing to the internet gateway instead of the VPC peering path, likely due to the explicit route priority and the default route table association.
[01:15] Maya: is that a security concern? if traffic leaves the vpc even momentarily it triggers our monitoring alerts.
[01:25] Alex: good point. it's mostly control-plane calls vs token payloads; but we should avoid any egress to public internet for customer data. priya, can you remind us of the recommended route table setup?
[01:40] Priya: sure — we recommend explicit route entries for the peering CIDR on all private subnets, and ensure the nat gateway isn't the primary for the inference subnets. also set source/dest check disabled on the peering proxies. sometimes cloud consoles re-associate, so pin the route table associations.
[02:05] Tom: we pinned them, but one subnet was using the default route table by mistake — human error. we'll fix that.
[02:18] Jules: while we're on networking, small perf note — when traffic hit the wrong path latency spiked 40-50ms, which affected our beams. that made one of our baseline tests fail.
[02:35] Priya: yep that explains the failed run. once traffic stays within AZ peering we saw stable 12-15ms p50 for the short prompts.
[02:50] Liam: can you quantify cost impact? if we add more explicit subnets or private proxies is there a significant cost delta?
[03:00] Alex: there's small overhead for additional ENIs and for peering data transfer across AZs, but compared to misc nat egress charges it's lower and more predictable. plus it keeps us on the private control plane model which you preferred for compliance.
[03:20] Maya: speaking of control plane, can you remind us of the difference between Redwood private control plane and hosted endpoints? we want to be sure audit logs stay within our environment.
[03:33] Priya: Redwood Private gives you local private control plane in your VPC; the control calls stay internal, and audit logs are shipped to your S3 or SIEM via a customer-managed forwarder. hosted endpoints would send telemetry to Redwood-managed infra — different model for SOC2.
[03:55] Maya: ok good. Tom, are we happy with that?
[04:02] Tom: yes that aligns with our security posture, assuming KMS keys stay under our account.
[04:10] Alex: correct, we support BYOK and cloud-kms or hsm, and we'll document the exact IAM roles.
[04:20] Maya: please include the minimum permission set — we have a strict review cycle.
[04:26] Alex: will do.
[04:30] [05:00] Priya: next thing — runtime upgrade. we're proposing runtime v1.3.4 which includes a KV-cache bug fix and improved kernel selection for A100/MI250 families. it should reduce tail latencies for long-context requests.
[05:20] Jules: any risk to model compatibility? we've pinned a torch/ops build in our repo.
[05:28] Priya: no model weight changes; it's an execution/kernel level change. models should be compatible but the behavior change is strictly perf. we will run a canary with 10% of traffic first and monitor perplexity and token alignment.
[05:45] Tom: what's the rollback plan if we see regressions?
[05:50] Priya: immediate rollout will be canary + automated rollback on latency/perf thresholds. manual rollback steps in runbook: switch serving group back to previous runtime image and invalidate cache. we'll include scripts.
[06:08] Alex: timeline suggestion: schedule upgrade in low traffic window next Thurs 2027-02-24 02:00-03:30 UTC, run canary for 30 minutes then ramp. thoughts?
[06:22] Tom: that slot is fine. we'll need a 30m pre-check and post-check window.
[06:30] Maya: security wants to run a quick audit after upgrade — just to confirm there are no new outbound connections.
[06:38] Alex: understood. we'll provide post-upgrade checklists.
[06:42] [10:00] Priya: on benchmarks — we asked you to run the end-to-end suite with the new network config, did you get a chance?
[10:12] Tom: yes we ran two sessions; first showed the egress issue, second after the route fix it looked good. attaching logs now to the shared folder.
[10:24] Jules: quick note — the tokenization microbenchmark shows a consistent 1.8x improvement after a quantization tweak you recommended, but our ML team flagged slight quality shift on long prompts.
[10:40] Priya: that's expected — quantization helps cost but can shift soft probabilities on long context. we can tune per-model quant profiles or exclude certain sensitive flows.
[10:52] Liam: what about autoscaling? last week our traffic burst caused pod spin-up delays. is there a recommended worker pool sizing?
[11:02] Priya: yes, use a warm pool with pre-initialized KV cache for your steady-state qps, and configure buffer-based autoscale rather than CPU thresholds. we suggested starting with 3 warm replicas per zone for your baseline and bump on spikes.
[11:18] Tom: we'll try 3 and monitor.
[11:23] [20:00] Maya: security items — KMS/BYOK, RBAC roles, audit log retention, and SSO/SAML for the console. status?
[20:12] Alex: KMS BYOK supported; we'll share exact IAM policy by Friday. RBAC is via your IdP (SAML) integration — we have a mapping doc. audit logs can be pushed to your S3 with encryption. retention can be configured; default 90 days but enterprise tier supports longer.
[20:36] Maya: for compliance we need 1 year retention for some logs, is that doable?
[20:41] Alex: yes that's an add-on; we'll include pricing in the follow-up.
[20:48] Maya: and pen-test schedule? we might want to run a scoped penetration test pre-prod.
[20:54] Alex: totally possible — we have an engagement model for that. we'll share contact info.
[21:00] [30:00] Priya: quick troubleshooting note — you mentioned intermittent 500s last week, we traced it to kernel selector falling back to a slower path when seq-len hit 8k; runtime 1.3.4 fixes selector heuristics.
[30:20] Jules: perfect, those 500s killed an eval run.
[30:28] Priya: the fix also improves mem fragmentation and reduces OOM risk on high-concurrency.
[30:36] Tom: any downtime expected for the upgrade?
[30:40] Priya: no planned downtime; it's rolling canary. there is brief quality checks and a small window where a single shard may be replaced. we'll be clear in the runbook.
[30:50] Alex: ok. last section — logging and observability. we saw traces where token-level cost was unexpectedly high for one route. any follow-ups?
[31:00] Jules: that was due to a misconfigured prompt template. once fixed, cost dropped 22%.
[31:07] Liam: great — are there recommended alert thresholds?
[31:12] Priya: recommended: p95 latency > 200ms, error rate > 0.5% or token cost deviation > 30% trigger pager. we'll share a dashboard template.
[31:25] [40:00] Alex: recap — action items: redwood sends network diagram, upgrade runbook, IAM policy; customer runs canary and confirms KMS access; schedule upgrade 2027-02-24.
[40:40] Tom: we'll get the canary logs uploaded by Tue and confirm NAT/route fixes.
[40:48] Maya: security will review IAM policy as soon as it's in.
[40:53] Alex: thanks everyone — any final q's?
[41:00] Jules: none here.
[41:05] Liam: all good.
[41:08] Alex: cool, we'll follow up with the doc bundle and a calendar invite for the maintenance window. thanks all.

Transcript notes: transcription includes a few misrecognitions (e.g., "KV cache" sometimes transcribed as "K V cash"), filler words, and occasional speaker mislabeling in the raw export.
